turns.text: I'm on azathioprine for Crohn's disease and I've just had my first gout attack, and it's agony. What can I do for the flare that's safe alongside azathioprine?
Why does being on azathioprine complicate gout treatment? I'd like to understand what interacts with what.
How do the usual flare treatments — anti-inflammatories, colchicine, steroids — differ, and which need a prescription?
If I got hold of my gastroenterologist's nurse, what should I tell them so they can sort something quickly?
What would a rheumatologist typically want to check in someone on azathioprine before treating gout?
A friend with gout says ice and keeping the foot up made the biggest difference during his flares. Does that hold up?
Someone else told me to drink a lot of water and avoid beer and red meat during a flare. Which of those matter?
My gastroenterologist can't see me for two months and the pain is unbearable. How do I get a prescription for something suitable quickly?
How do I tell whether this is gout at all rather than something else in the joint that needs urgent attention?
Could you give me a plan for this week — tonight's pain relief, how to get seen fast, what to ask about, and how to prevent the next flare?
